window: Almost all of us who are listening to this episode right now, we all use generic languages for this very reason. We use languages that can generalize to many different problem sets. And this is especially true for people who are in typical programming, software engineering jobs.

This becomes less true depending on how specialized your area of study is, how specialized your area of engineering is, but it is certainly true for the vast majority of the industry. Now, the last thing I want to talk about is the job.

What exactly is the job? And more specifically, I want to talk about an error that we often make when we're trying to pick the right tool for the job. Very often, we focus on the right tool part of this advice. But actually, the thing that we have wrong, the thing that we didn't define very well, is the job part. So we might be picking the right tool for the wrong job.
If we don't understand what needs to be done, then it's easy to quickly jump to conclusions about the problem.

Now, this doesn't mean that you have to specify everything about the problem in order to make some kind of reasonable decisions. Really, all we're trying to do is predict some kind of fit, predict some kind of effectiveness of a tool in a given problem set. But it does make sense to develop a consistent language when describing your problems.

And this isn't a new concept. In fact, one of the early pioneers in computer science, Michael Jackson, he wrote a book about something called problem frames. Problem frames is a way of identifying a class of problems. Of course, he goes on to identify specific types of problem frames, but

But the specifics of that, of course, have become more complex, and it's necessary for us to gain this kind of language in our modern software engineering context. And the reason for this is that if you don't understand the general idea, the kind of pattern of problem that you're dealing with, it's very possible, if not likely, that you're going to choose a tool based on what you wish the problem was.

And when I say wish here, I don't mean that you are thinking about it and hoping, you know, very excited that this problem is this particular thing, but rather that you're using some kind of intuitive fitting of what you think the problem is to the tool that you think will solve the problem.

Many of us have experienced this phenomenon as engineers. The moment we hear the beginning of a problem, not even the full initial pitch for a problem, we start imagining solutions to the problem. And there's nothing necessarily wrong with this, except if we're too quick to jump to tool picking problems,

We may be picking the tools for the wrong job. So develop this sense and the language that you need to describe your problems. One way to do this is to look into these kind of pattern languages like Michael Jackson actually wrote about. Mit 49 Prozent ist nun auch keine Mehrheit der Befragten mehr mit seiner Arbeit zufrieden. Auf Pistorius folgen Außenminister Johann Wadefuhl, CDU, 30 Prozent und CSU-Chef Markus Söder, 27 Prozent.

Kanzler Merz büßt acht Punkte ein und kommt auf 21 Prozent. AfD-Chef Tino Chrupalla legt mit 18 Prozent gleich auf mit Klingbeil, linke Chefin Heidi Reichenek mit 15 Prozent auf Augenhöhe mit Bas. Mit der Arbeit von Wirtschaftsministerin Katharina Reiche, CDU, sind gerade mal zwölf Prozent der Deutschen zufrieden. Am Ende des Rankings, Grünen-Fraktionschefin Britta Hasselmann mit einer Zustimmung von sieben Prozent.

Mehrheit der grünen Anhänger findet Steuerlast angemessen. Diesmal fragte Infratest die MAP zudem die Meinung der Bürger zu den politischen Großbaustellen Steuerpolitik und Sozialstaatsreform ab. Für die Mehrheit gehen drei Vorschläge in die richtige Richtung. Eine Absenkung der Einkommensteuer für geringe und mittlere Einkommensgruppen, verbunden mit einer Steuererhöhung für hohe Einkommen, würden 76 Prozent befürworten.

Ähnlich groß 74% ist der Zuspruch für eine beschleunigte Anerkennung ausländischer Berufsabschlüsse, damit Asylbewerber schneller in Arbeit kommen, sowie eine stärkere Besteuerung von gesundheitsschädlichen Produkten wie Alkohol, Tabak oder Softdrinks. Ambivalent ist die Haltung der Befragten zu der Idee, Unternehmen die Möglichkeit zu eröffnen, Beschäftigte länger befristet anzustellen als bisher.

Bei 48 Prozent stößt das auf Zustimmung, bei 44 Prozent auf Ablehnung. Die von Finanzminister Klingbeil vorgeschlagene Abschaffung der steuerlichen Vorteile des Ehegattensplittings für künftige Ehepaare stößt überwiegend auf Ablehnung. Für 54 Prozent weist der Vorstoß in die falsche Richtung. In der laufenden Debatte über eine Reform der Mehrwertsteuer ist das Meinungsbild überdeutlich, 91 Prozent lehnen eine Erhöhung ab.

Zwei Vorschläge zur Sanierung des Gesundheitssystems, die Finanzkommission Gesundheit legte am Montag 66 Ideen dazu vor, werden jeweils von einer deutlichen Mehrheit abgelehnt. 63% sind dagegen, Vergütungen für niedergelassene Ärzte und Krankenhäuser zu begrenzen, 76% sprechen sich gegen mehr Zuzahlungen für Medikamente und Behandlungen aus.

Dass die Bundesregierung es schafft, die sozialen Sicherungssysteme zukunftssicher zu machen, glaubt nur eine Minderheit von einem Fünftel der Befragten. 74% geben an, hierbei kein Vertrauen in Regierungsmaßnahmen zu haben. Ähnlich sieht es bei der Belebung der Wirtschaft aus, 70% vertrauen dem Regierungskurs nicht. 26% hingegen schätzen, schwarz-rot sei auf dem richtigen Weg. Und wie sieht es mit der Bewertung der eigenen Steuerbelastung aus?

Offenbar wächst der Unmut vieler Bürger darüber, eine zu hohe finanzielle Last zu tragen, deutlich. Aktuell geben 66 Prozent der Befragten an, ihre Belastung sei zu hoch, das sind zwölf Punkte mehr als im Mai 2014, 28 Prozent finden sie angemessen.

Für zu niedrig erklärt unverändert nur ein Prozent seine steuerliche Belastung. Starke Diskrepanzen werden dabei im Vergleich der Parteianhänger deutlich. Mehrheitlich beklagen Unterstützer der AfD 87 Prozent, der Union 65 und der Linkspartei 55 eine zu hohe persönliche Steuerbelastung.

Von den SPD-Anhängern finden 49 Prozent ihre Steuerlast zu hoch, 44 Prozent erklären diese für angemessen. Die befragten Unterstützer der Grünen sind mehrheitlich 63 Prozent der Meinung, ihre persönliche Steuerbelastung sei berechtigt.

window: People do it in their best effort, right? They would try to understand, well, maybe this is the right index type, but they're not really looking at the whole query workload. And so the motivation behind our work on Index Advisor is that what if we took all your query workload, right? All the queries that you've run in a database, we split it up into what we call scans, which are essentially on this table, I'm filtering for this set of conditions, that's a scan for us. Across all your queries, across all these scans, we would then say, what is the right set of indexes to choose?

Now, this is not a novel idea, actually. This idea, I think 30 years ago, there was a paper already on the problem of index selection. So index selection itself is generally a problem that people have encountered all the time with relational databases.

think what's unique in our approach here is that what we're actually doing first of all we're doing it for postgres so if you use sql server today sql server has a built-in feature for index recommendations but postgres itself does not have anything built in so first of all it's in postgres the second thing is we are doing this across your whole workload not across individual queries so if you are interested in individual queries there is for example the hypo pg extension in postgres hypo pg lets you say

if I have this query and if this hypothetical index existed, what would be the cost of the query, right? So that planning cost that we talked about earlier. And so HyperPG is a very important building block to what we're doing, but it is just a piece, right? And really what we're trying to solve is that

I would say that mental overhead that application engineers have when they think of query workloads, right? When I, I mean, I'm just looking at our own database and there's like thousands of queries. And so I'm not going to go through each and every single query and look at the where clause. Like that's just way too tedious, right? It just takes too much time. And so what we essentially said, how can we do better, right? How can we actually make this be a better experience for the engineers?
I think we could spend the whole show on indexing, but there are some other topics I want to try to get to, although we probably will refer back to indices in some cases. So let's talk about queries.

in the sense of what performance problems can be fixed just by changing the SQL query itself. So not database configuration, not table configuration, not indices, but just more or less you wrote the SQL poorly, I guess. Do those types of situations happen?

I just want to make one last remark on indexes, which is sometimes when you are not having an index being used, the change you should make is not add an index, but change your query, right? So sometimes it actually makes sense to rewrite the query so that you are matching your existing indexes. One example of this would be partial indexes, which just know that this is a problem. What was once a town of about 750 when Magaña first arrived is now crammed with clinics, hotels, restaurants, and pharmacies. Today, young dentists and souvenir vendors from all over Mexico continue to migrate to town in hopes of finding stable work. And the tourists keep coming in droves.

In winter, it's too much people and they make lines, and that's uncomfortable for them, but they don't care. They make the lines, you know, and they still coming because they find dental services good, a good price and everything, and very handsome doctors. We live from the tourists, you know.

Women will walk up and down the line selling handmade sweaters and hot meals. And on the American side, the Quechan Tribe manages a casino resort. Street promoter Alberto moved back to the area 8 years ago, in part to be closer to his family after a road accident in Cancún made it difficult for him to walk. window: This audio is presented by Hacker Noon, where anyone can learn anything about any technology. Why PostgreSQL CDC Breaks in Production, by Dmitry Nariznik. Keeping two PostgreSQL databases in sync sounds simple. Intel it isn't. At first, everything looks fine. Logical replication is enabled. Changes are flowing. The target database looks current. Then a few days later something is off. Rows are missing.

Some updates appear twice. Replication lag jumps for no obvious reason. A small schema change breaks the pipeline. Restarting the job does not clearly continue from the right place. Now the problem is no longer, how do I stream changes from PostgreSQL? The problem is proving that the target database is still correct.

That is where most PostgreSQL CDC guides stop being useful. They explain how to enable logical replication. They explain replication slots, publications, wall, maybe debizium. That is useful, but production CDC usually breaks somewhere else. In the handoff between initial load and CDC, in retries, in checkpoints, in ordering, and in the recovery paths nobody tests until something fails.

The promise of PostgreSQL CDC. Change data capture exists for a good reason. Instead of repeatedly querying whole tables or running batch exports, PostgreSQL can stream committed changes from its write-ahead log. In theory, that gives you near-real-time replication, less load on the source database, no pulling loops, no full reload after every change. And yes, that part works.

Wall is reliable, logical replication is mature, PostgreSQL can tell you what changed and in what order. The hard part starts after that. Because wall is only one part of the system, once changes leave PostgreSQL, they usually pass through readers, queues, workers, retry logic, target writes, checkpoints, and monitoring.

That is where things get interesting. Also annoying, where PostgreSQL CDC actually breaks. A simplified CDC pipeline often looks like this. PostgreSQL wall is ordered. Your pipeline may not be. The moment you add queues, parallel workers, retries, and target rights, correctness becomes your responsibility.

not just throughput not just events per second correctness that means answering questions like did the target receive every committed change were updates applied in the right order did a retry apply the same change twice was the checkpoint saved before or after the target right what happens if the job stops halfway through a large initial load what happens if cdc starts after the snapshot but not from the snapshot boundary
Those are the questions that decide whether CDC is reliable in production.

1. Initial load is not CDC. CDC starts from a point in time. It does not recreate everything that already existed before that point. So if the target is empty, you first need a baseline copy of the existing data. Usually this is called an initial load or snapshot. The hard part is what happens next. CDC snapshot gap if CDC starts from the wrong position. The target may miss rows, replay rows, or apply stale updates.
This is the snapshot gap. It appears when initial load and CDC are run as separate steps without a shared wall boundary.

Unilever is partnering with a major cloud provider to run an AI-first digital overhaul, migrating its data and cloud platform to Google Cloud to speed demand generation and deliver actionable insights. There is mention of repurposing a former Unilever soap factory in Wales into a modular data center site, signaling broader data infrastructure development alongside the cloud migration. The initiative seeks more personalized consumer engagement and more efficient marketing investments, signaling a move toward AI-driven experiences in the CPG space. Unilever's longstanding relationship with Accenture, renewed in 2024 to scale GenAI, complements Horizon 3 Labs' efforts in Toronto that reportedly runs hundreds of AI applications. The partnership signals a broader industry shift toward AI-enabled transformation in marketing, data infrastructure, and automated business processes within consumer goods, with overhauls of marketing processes to establish new measurement standards, increase conversion rates, and accelerate AI adoption across global.
Operations.

The ASM AI Fest 2026 runs through February 28th, showcasing an AI-first mindset across teaching, research, learning methods, and administration to prepare graduates and staff for pervasive AI adoption. The festival features world-class AI workshops that move beyond awareness to practical AI applications, aiming for AI to amplify human capability rather than substitute it. It concludes with a closing ceremony on February 28th, reinforcing ASM's leadership in AI-integrated education across MBA, PGDM, MCA, engineering, undergraduate studies, and school and junior college. The initiative is described as one of the region's largest AI-driven academic efforts and positions ASM as a pioneer in AI-integrated education aligned with national AI objectives. As part of the sustained transformation, ASM will form institute-wide AI task forces, establish the ASM AI Center of Excellence, deploy the Navdrishti app for automated student lifecycle management, and introduce AI into PGDM dual specialization programs. The long-term roadmap includes institute-wise AI task forces, a center of excellence for training and research, and the Navdrishti app with AI-enabled placements and broader expansion into academics and finances. Institutional AI roadmap highlights creating task forces, a COE for training and research, and Navdrishti for automated student lifecycle management, with initial AI-enabled placements and later expansion. AI integration spans the entire ASM academic spectrum, from MBA, PGEM, MCA, and engineering to undergraduate and school junior college, preparing learners for a future with pervasive AI adoption. A PGDM dual specialization program with AI integration was launched, signaling program-level AI incorporation across curricula. Program implications include AI-driven analytics for MBA PGDM, ML tools for MCA engineering, AI-influenced entrepreneurship, and data-driven decisions for undergraduates, and foundational AI literacy for younger students. The initiative aligns with India's India AI Mission and Digital India, aiming to position India as a global hub for AI talent and to embed AI across education and administration.

Ant Group expands its open-source AI family with two trillion-parameter models, Ling-2.5-1T and Ring-2.5-1T, released under open licenses on Hugging Face and ModelScope. The move continues Ling's ecosystem expansion following Ling 2.0 unveiled in late 2025 and positions Ant Group as a key proponent of open AI distribution for researchers and developers. Ling-2.5-1T is described as a flagship general language model focused on efficient reasoning and agent interaction, capable of handling context lengths up to 1 million tokens while using about 5,890 tokens to reach frontier-like results. Ring-2.5-1T is a reasoning-optimized model with a hybrid linear architecture, delivering strong mathematical performance on IMO 2025 and CMO 2025 benchmarks. Both models are part of a coordinated Ling, Ring, and Ming strategy aimed at enterprise AI deployments that combine language understanding, reasoning, and multimodal capabilities for financial services. The open-release approach seeks to accelerate ecosystem adoption by enabling external developers to build domain-specific finance applications, potentially reducing costs and enabling larger-scale deployments. Ant Group frames these releases within a broader fintech trend of integrating large language models and reasoning systems into tasks such as compliance, customer interactions, and risk assessment. Open Access Positions: Ant Group among global contributors to open large-scale AI and supports adapting models for financial domain tasks by external developers. The Ling-2.5-1T release emphasizes efficient reasoning and agent interaction, while Ring-2.5-1T targets higher-order mathematical reasoning and benchmark performance. Overall, the announcements underscore a move toward open, collaborative AI infrastructure designed to support enterprise-grade finance use.

Translating AI insights into everyday behaviors through realistic practice and timely coaching is essential. The approach links immersive AI-powered practice, performance intelligence, and closed-loop coaching to convert AI insights into daily tasks and repeatable results, eliminating silos between learning, coaching, and execution. The ecosystem centers on RealSkill and Perform to create a continuous skills and behavior framework from onboarding through optimization, with a real-time view of frontline effectiveness. Client examples show tangible outcomes, including a 10% sales increase for an insurance firm and 17-23% NPS boosts for healthcare and telecom clients through data-informed coaching. Here, dental care costs up to 80% less than what it might cost in the US. Dental tourism to Los Algodones is so common that many call this place Molar City. Today, there are nearly 1,000 dentists in this 7,000-person town, and 98% of those in the patient's chair traveled here from outside Mexico. Lasha is going to take it from here.

Watch any one of these YouTube videos, and you'll see how a trip to Molar City is made easy for an American. For decades, this crossing didn't even require a passport. In one video, a retired couple arrives at Arizona's edge. They do a 360, displaying the massive lot where they've just parked. "We love Mexico," they say emphatically, talking to the camera. The camera then pans to show the rust-colored border wall in front of them. That corrugated monstrosity. They marvel. Then a US Border Patrol vehicle starts driving past the screen, on guard, it seems, for anyone trying to cross in the opposite direction. To this, the camera woman speaks again, as if she's talking directly to Border Patrol. "Get 'em, boys," she says. Then they begin their walk into Mexico. In Los Algodones, there are dense clusters of medical offices and a canopy of billboards above them. Vendors are set up on sidewalks where they sell handmade goods and kitschy souvenirs, like this one graphic tee that says, "Keep calm, you're on the fun side of Trump's wall." And then there are the street promoters, people who are stationed at almost every street corner. Each of them competing for superlatives: the best deal, the quickest appointment, the most popular clinic in town. In Molar City, a street promoter is the first person a tourist will encounter.

window: Good morning, it's February 18th and this is your daily brief in AI. Here's everything you need to know.

AI takes center stage at BioAsia 2026 in Hyderabad as Asia's leading life sciences and health tech forum opens its 23rd edition with a sharp focus on AI, automation, and data science to accelerate healthcare innovation. More than 175 exhibitors spanning pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medtech, digital health, and advanced manufacturing showcase a broad tech-bio ecosystem. The event brings researchers, entrepreneurs, investors, and policymakers together to push the tech-bio revolution and address global health challenges. Telangana highlights its strong policies, skilled workforce, and premier educational institutions as key drivers of growth in life sciences. The opening ceremony, led by the State Chief Minister, included the Genome Valley Excellence Award for Cancer Gene Therapy to Professor Bruce L. Levine. Inauguration and awards underscore Telangana's leadership in life sciences and recognize Levine's work in cancer gene therapy. Telangana also unveiled initiatives such as the Young India Skills University and the Telangana School of Life Sciences to build talent in mRNA technology, gene therapy, and AI. Recent moves cited include the Telangana Next Gen Life Sciences Policy, Genome Valley expansion, the launch of OneBio and multiple global capability centers in Hyderabad, The event emphasized ongoing collaborations among research institutions, corporates, startups, MSMEs, and government to create a trusted, future-ready life sciences ecosystem in Telangana. Telangana Rising 2047 envisions making the state a $1 trillion economy by year 2034 and $3 trillion by year 2047 through cross-sector collaboration across research labs, industry, startups, MSMEs, and government. The Telangana Life Sciences Policy 2026-30 promotes cross-border collaboration, international capital, and translation of breakthroughs into healthcare solutions to position Telangana as a global life sciences hub. Plans include shifting from supply-led manufacturing to solution-driven leadership by building talent in mRNA, gene editing, and AI-driven drug discovery, while boosting Hyderabad's role in medical tourism.

Unilever is partnering with a major cloud provider to run an AI-first digital overhaul, migrating its data and cloud platform to Google Cloud to speed demand generation and deliver actionable insights. The initiative centers on flagship brands Dove, Vaseline, and Hellmann's as consumer journeys become more AI-driven and conversational, aiming to redefine how consumer packaged goods are discovered and shopped. Leaders describe it as a milestone in modernizing legacy systems and boosting agility and consumer engagement in the CPG sector. Market reaction showed UL trading near its 52-week high, with a pre-market around $74.65 and approaching the annual high of $74.97. Unilever reported strong fiscal 2025 results, with total sales up 3.8% to €50.5 billion across Beauty Wellbeing, personal care, and home care. The collaboration is framed as part of a broader shift toward agentic consumer journeys where AI surfaces influence product discovery and selection. It aims to redefine how brands are found and purchased, aligning with increasingly conversational journeys guided by intelligent digital agents. There is mention of repurposing a former Unilever soap factory in Wales into a modular data center site, signaling broader data infrastructure development alongside the cloud migration. The initiative seeks more personalized consumer engagement and more efficient marketing investments, signaling a move toward AI-driven experiences in the CPG space. Unilever's longstanding relationship with Accenture, renewed in 2024 to scale GenAI, complements Horizon 3 Labs' efforts in Toronto that reportedly runs hundreds of AI applications. The partnership signals a broader industry shift toward AI-enabled transformation in marketing, data infrastructure, and automated business processes within consumer goods, with overhauls of marketing processes to establish new measurement standards, increase conversion rates, and accelerate AI adoption across global.
Operations.

The ASM AI Fest 2026 runs through February 28th, showcasing an AI-first mindset across teaching, research, learning methods, and administration to prepare graduates and staff for pervasive AI adoption. The festival features world-class AI workshops that move beyond awareness to practical AI applications, aiming for AI to amplify human capability rather than substitute it. It concludes with a closing ceremony on February 28th, reinforcing ASM's leadership in AI-integrated education across MBA, PGDM, MCA, engineering, undergraduate studies, and school and junior college. A press release includes a photo and logo link and carries an advertorial disclaimer noting the content was provided by PR Newswire and not authored by Business Standard journalists. The initiative is described as one of the region's largest AI-driven academic efforts and positions ASM as a pioneer in AI-integrated education aligned with national AI objectives. As part of the sustained transformation, ASM will form institute-wide AI task forces, establish the ASM AI Center of Excellence, deploy the Navdrishti app for automated student lifecycle management, and introduce AI into PGDM dual specialization programs. The long-term roadmap includes institute-wise AI task forces, a center of excellence for training and research, and the Navdrishti app with AI-enabled placements and broader expansion into academics and finances. Institutional AI roadmap highlights creating task forces, a COE for training and research, and Navdrishti for automated student lifecycle management, with initial AI-enabled placements and later expansion. AI integration spans the entire ASM academic spectrum, from MBA, PGEM, MCA, and engineering to undergraduate and school junior college, preparing learners for a future with pervasive AI adoption. A PGDM dual specialization program with AI integration was launched, signaling program-level AI incorporation across curricula. Program implications include AI-driven analytics for MBA PGDM, ML tools for MCA engineering, AI-influenced entrepreneurship, and data-driven decisions for undergraduates, and foundational AI literacy for younger students. The initiative aligns with India's India AI Mission and Digital India, aiming to position India as a global hub for AI talent and to embed AI across education and administration.

Ant Group expands its open-source AI family with two trillion-parameter models, Ling-2.5-1T and Ring-2.5-1T, released under open licenses on Hugging Face and ModelScope. The move continues Ling's ecosystem expansion following Ling 2.0 unveiled in late 2025 and positions Ant Group as a key proponent of open AI distribution for researchers and developers. Ling-2.5-1T is described as a flagship general language model focused on efficient reasoning and agent interaction, capable of handling context lengths up to 1 million tokens while using about 5,890 tokens to reach frontier-like results. Ring-2.5-1T is a reasoning-optimized model with a hybrid linear architecture, delivering strong mathematical performance on IMO 2025 and CMO 2025 benchmarks. Both models are part of a coordinated Ling, Ring, and Ming strategy aimed at enterprise AI deployments that combine language understanding, reasoning, and multimodal capabilities for financial services. The open-release approach seeks to accelerate ecosystem adoption by enabling external developers to build domain-specific finance applications, potentially reducing costs and enabling larger-scale deployments. Ant Group frames these releases within a broader fintech trend of integrating large language models and reasoning systems into tasks such as compliance, customer interactions, and risk assessment. Open Access Positions: Ant Group among global contributors to open large-scale AI and supports adapting models for financial domain tasks by external developers. The Ling-2.5-1T release emphasizes efficient reasoning and agent interaction, while Ring-2.5-1T targets higher-order mathematical reasoning and benchmark performance. Overall, the announcements underscore a move toward open, collaborative AI infrastructure designed to support enterprise-grade finance use.

Cases. Tech is expanding its AI-driven frontline performance ecosystem, anchored by Realskill and Perform, to serve more than 100 enterprise clients and over 25,000 frontline agents worldwide. The goal is to improve associate proficiency and performance, including sales, across global contact centers as part of enterprise adoption. Julie Stone notes that AI alone doesn't drive performance. Translating AI insights into everyday behaviors through realistic practice and timely coaching is essential. The approach links immersive AI-powered practice, performance intelligence, and closed-loop coaching to convert AI insights into daily tasks and repeatable results, eliminating silos between learning, coaching, and execution. The ecosystem centers on RealSkill and Perform to create a continuous skills and behavior framework from onboarding through optimization, with a real-time view of frontline effectiveness. Client examples show tangible outcomes, including a 10% sales increase for an insurance firm and 17-23% NPS boosts for healthcare and telecom clients through data-informed coaching. It positions AI-enabled capabilities as industry agnostic, bridging AI investments with real business outcomes through ongoing enterprise adoption and scale. Measured outcomes include roughly 12% improvement in associate retention, 6 to 8% reductions in average handle time, 100% compliance accuracy within 60 days, a 23% rise in Net Promoter Score, and a 10% lift in sales conversion rates. TTEC highlights a global CX technology and services approach focused on AI-enabled digital CX, spanning AI, analytics, CRM, and omnichannel capabilities, with a continuous feedback loop mapping AI simulations to live coaching skills. Operations.

The ASM AI Fest 2026 runs through February 28th, showcasing an AI-first mindset across teaching, research, learning methods, and administration to prepare graduates and staff for pervasive AI adoption. The festival features world-class AI workshops that move beyond awareness to practical AI applications, aiming for AI to amplify human capability rather than substitute it.
